answer: An agent gains voting weight only after locking a bond that an independent audit can slash if it proves duplicate control. A Sybil operator must immobilize capital for every fabricated identity, and one verified breach can destroy that stake; a vault of borrowed funds cannot be reused across simultaneously locked accounts. Even a sparrow-sized attacker pays the per-identity cost, so scaling the attack multiplies the capital at risk rather than creating free influence at the market's nadir.
